purpose: Belimumab is used to treat adults and some children with active lupus (also called systemic lupus erythematosus, or SLE). It is also used for a type of kidney disease caused by lupus called lupus nephritis. It helps reduce lupus flares and control symptoms like joint pain, rashes, and fatigue.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes proteins called B cells, which can sometimes mistakenly attack your own body in lupus. Belimumab blocks a specific protein called BLyS that helps these overactive B cells survive. By blocking this protein, it reduces the number of harmful B cells and calms down the immune system's attack on your body.
common_side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, and upset stomach are fairly common. You may also experience headaches, fever, or trouble sleeping. Some people have reactions during or after their infusion or injection, such as redness, itching, or feeling flushed.
warnings: Because belimumab lowers part of your immune system, you have a higher chance of getting serious infections — contact your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, or signs of infection. It may increase the risk of depression, anxiety, or rarely, thoughts of self-harm, so tell your doctor if your mood changes. Do not use live vaccines while on this medication. It is not recommended during pregnancy, so discuss reliable birth control with your doctor.
typical_dosing: Belimumab can be given in two ways: as an intravenous (IV) infusion at a clinic — usually 10 mg per kg of body weight once a month after three starter doses given two weeks apart — or as a weekly injection under the skin (subcutaneous) at home using a prefilled autoinjector at a dose of 200 mg. Your doctor will decide which method is best for you.
